items.title: What the paper claims after campaign 26, and which arm is the baseline of record, was recommended to the user and not answered
items.what_is_undone: On 12 Nov the lead told the user that at 44 users and 70 GB the forecast buys SSD traffic, not latency, and that the baseline of record should be the no-hint, queue-aware engine (against it '2.9x from exact hints' becomes 1.4x). Later arms sharpened this: rule 3 moves TTFT in neither row, the learned price buys nothing, rule 2 costs SSD pages, rule 1's lead over the no-hint rival is not shown, and exact hints lead it by 0.14-0.21 s (shown). The user asked follow-up questions but never said which claim or baseline the paper takes. PAPER_PLAN.md:210-213 lists 'Which result leads' among the author's open decisions, and campaign 26 changes the candidates. The doc rewrite is held (U78-U90); this is the decision underneath it.

The lead put it to the user at 01:42Z on 12 Nov as decision 2 of three (the no-hint rival, rules 1+3, JIT exact, original HiCache) and restated it at 02:33Z and 02:39Z; the user's reply was 'Let's keep these running, no furthere action for now.' It dropped out of the pending lists after 18:57Z on 12 Nov and is not in K2. Nothing exists: every launch in launcher.log is 'gap 10'. Campaign 18 ran this setting for original HiCache and the old oracle only (1.09 and 0.58 s). The intro's problem statement and contributions 1 and 2 rest on x70 numbers (the campaign 16 ablation 18.5 -> 13.2 -> 11.6 -> 5.7 s) measured before the no-hint rival existed; at x10 the read thread is 16-20 % busy. Today's pool-sweep entry says the CPU model cannot place such a setting. Effort: 4 arms; 2 h each at the queue's length, 5 h by the memory note of 1 Nov for an x70 run.

items.title: Third setting: the deck's choice would have nothing to read; no setting is queued where the rules can act with room for ten histories
items.what_is_undone: Deck step 4 names 'a third setting with fewer users at 160 GB'; the review's fix for the theory (weak spot 8) was a setting where the room holds ten or more histories. Done instead: 100 GB at 44 users for three non-pricing arms. The cut run and the pool sweep say that at 100 GB under 1 % of returning turns read from SSD and at 160 GB 0.2-0.3 %, so neither the deck's setting nor a pricing arm at 100 GB or 136 GB would give the rules reads to time. Open and not queued: a pool of 75-85 GB at 44 users (2.7-10.8 % of turns read under LRU by the sweep; by one reader's arithmetic, which is in no file, ten histories of 17-19K tokens need a pool of about 84 GB), or more users per GB with a short GPU queue (U42). Never put to the user in this form.
items.sources: Finders: deck, transcript-requests, transcript-promises; notes of record-1. Deck slide next 'a third setting with fewer users at 160 GB'; DECISIONS.md:30, :1074, :1100 ('| LRU (no hints) | 17.0 % | 9.4-10.8 | 4.9-6.7 | 2.7-4.2 | 1.5-2.7 | 0.8-1.2 | 0.6-0.8 | 0.2-0.3 |', 70 to 160 GB), :1110-1113; transcript 25075 (2026-11-11T13:30Z: 'I have not queued another setting; the deck's planned third one is where rule 1 would have to show its worth.').
items.why_who: Which setting to add, if any, is a queue change. Each arm is 2 h.

verdict.evidence: The deck's wording is real: local copy scratchpad/artifact-files/728cef5b-413e-4529-8bd7-8056e39b919f/project/slides/next.html:32 'a third setting with fewer users at 160 GB'; DECISIONS.md:30 gives weak spot 8's fix as 'add a setting where the room holds ten or more'. A substitute exists: the last three lines of queue.txt (44 users, 100 GB; none has a pricing flag). Room there is 349K tokens (DECISIONS.md:562-563), 18-20 histories of 17-19K (:293), but only 56 of 8,030 returning turns read (:1074) and read stall is 0.006 s per turn (:1081). The deck's form has nothing to read at x10: DECISIONS.md:561-562 'at 160 GB no live session's history is on SSD and nothing is left to read early'; sweep :1100 gives LRU 0.2-0.3 % at 160 GB. The user was told so three times: idx 14160 (2026-11-01T02:35Z) 'Lowering the cap alone won't work, because it removes the SSD reads along with the queue'; idx 26376 (2026-11-12T02:39Z) 'A 160 GB pool holds 1,628K, more than the sessions ever hold, so nothing is on SSD'; idx 30745 (2026-11-13T19:46Z) '70 GB is already the setting most favourable to hints at 44 users' and '136 GB arm: I'd drop it'. items.title: Weak spot 4 ('Price more'): no queue or SSD price, no waiting for room, no fix written, no estimate of what waiting would buy
items.what_is_undone: The review's weak spot 4 says the cost leaves out the queue (a recomputed token costs 6-8 times its prefill) and SSD bandwidth; its row says 'not built' and the record writes no fix, though the request asked for a potential fix per weak spot (the one told to the user on 11 Nov, pricing recomputation by queue length so that a turn waits for room rather than recomputes, is not in the record). The engine has a flat recompute cost per token (next_turn_policy.py:44, RECOMPUTE_S_PER_TOKEN = 1.1e-4); only the harm price multiplies lost tokens by the queue length (next_turn_prefetch.py:1267-1269); read_start has no queue or SSD term and there is no waiting for room. PAPER_PLAN.md:135 lists the same gap as open, and the deck's second change prices GPU time at about (1 + Q)/rho per recomputed token. Later results bear on it: the largest remaining loss is 1 % of turns recomputing history after a refused read (123 returning turns in jit_exact_d, 113 in nofc_noend, about 11 s each, 14 % of all TTFT seconds; 58 turns had the read refused room, refusals mean 2.1, TTFT mean 10.3 s), and at 128 users seven arms are level on TTFT and differ only in SSD pages (998K to 1,441K), where a price on SSD bandwidth would decide. The SSD half looks unneeded at 44 users (read thread 16-20 % busy). No check estimates how long those turns would have waited for room and whether that beats recomputing behind a queue (CPU on existing logs, 1-2 h, if the user wants it).
items.sources: Finders: record-1, deck, transcript-promises, transcript-requests, code, leftovers, paper-plan. Would mean pricing recomputation by queue length, so a turn waits for room rather than recomputes.'); PAPER_PLAN.md:133-137; deck slide better ('With that price, waiting for room beats recomputing, and an early read must earn more.'); results/campaign26/checks/limits/why_recompute.out.
items.why_who: Building it means a change to the cost model, a new engine freeze and new arms: beyond the four rules, engines frozen during the campaign, the queue the user's. Writing the proposed fix into the closing review (U26) is the lead's to do. Effort: 30 min to write the fix; days to build and measure.

verdict.evidence:
The review part was delivered in chat; the build and the estimate do not exist.
1. The fix was given to the user but is not in the record: transcript 23049 (2026-11-11T04:35Z, review table row 6: 'Not built. Would mean pricing recomputation by queue length, so a turn waits for room rather than recomputes.'). DECISIONS.md:26 says only 'not built' (that table's column is 'In the build'), and 'bandwidth' occurs nowhere else in the file. So 'no fix written' is true of the record only.
2. Not built, by the code (both files are identical in the working tree and in frozen/engine_ec_20261111d and e): next_turn_policy.py:44, RECOMPUTE_S_PER_TOKEN = 1.1e-4, flat; read_start (:165-201) weighs stall against rent only, the queue wait just shifts the start; the queue length enters only the harm price (next_turn_prefetch.py:1267-1269, 'lost_tokens * RECOMPUTE_S_PER_TOKEN * max(1, queue_ahead)'); there is no SSD term.
3. What the engine does in place of a priced wait: retries are capped by a constant whatever the queue, MAX_REFETCHES = 2 (next_turn_prefetch.py:108, :878, :1332-1336, 'A re-read beats a recompute, but not without limit'). verdict.who_reason: Building it changes the cost model beyond the four rules and needs a new engine freeze and GPU arms. The offline estimate was never asked for. Only one piece is the lead's now: the request asked for a potential fix per weak spot, it needs no GPU, and DECISIONS.md is not on the held list, so the missing sentence can go into the record.
verdict.recommended_action: Now (5 minutes): put the 11 Nov fix sentence into the closing review (item U26) or row 4 of the review table, with the two code facts (flat recompute cost; retries capped at two by a constant). Then ask the user whether they want the estimate: a new script beside checks/limits/why_recompute.py that takes the capped and refused-room turns of nofc_noend and nofc_noend_rep and compares the time until the room could take the read (their ec_price lines give idle room every 5 s) with the recompute they paid, times one plus the queue. items.title: The three queue-state mechanisms behind the 1.0 s between the two hint-free arms are not separated
items.what_is_undone: The nofc entry says the rival adds four things to the hint-free arm, 'not yet separated' (L219). nofc_noend separated the end signal. The other three (queued turns' history kept, the arrival gate and hold, re-reads for queued turns) are still one bundle worth about 1.0 s at 44 users (paired +1.02 s on 9,703 turns) and 38.79 -> 20.84 s at 128 users. Exists: a split of that 1.02 s by which turns read from SSD, the count of turns that shrank while queued (9 against 288), and a bound on the hold's own cost (0.006-0.019 s per turn, L297). Missing: which mechanism carries the gain, by ablation arms or by an attribution on the logs. PAPER_PLAN.md:18 ('Where the gain comes from, one change at a time') still lists the 128-user ladder steps (three_tier_wc_oracle_v2 without next-use eviction, three_tier_wc_poll0) as not run. Gate and hold are server flags and queue lines take extra flags (scripts/start_server.sh:186-187), so such arms should need no engine edit; whether the engine accepts those flag combinations was not checked.
items.sources: Finders: record-1, paper-plan; notes of record-2 and leftovers (the reviewer asked for each mechanism alone). DECISIONS.md:219-221 ('**Against the hint-free arm it adds four things, not yet separated:** ended sessions evicted first, queued turns' history protected, the arrival gate and hold, and re-reads for queued turns.'), :297, :339-344; PAPER_PLAN.md:7, 18.
items.why_who: Ablation arms are the user's call (2-4 arms of 2 h per setting). An attribution on existing logs needs no GPU (1-2 h) but was not asked for. One reader said partial, one undone; kept undone.

verdict.evidence:
The three mechanisms are still one bundle in campaign 26, but more of the split exists than the claim lists.
1. Still bundled: DECISIONS.md:219-221 ('four things, not yet separated'), :339-344 (1.02 s on 9,703 shared turns), :595 and :600 (38.79 against 20.84 s at 128 users, across builds). No table sets gate decisions or refusals of the two hint-free arms side by side (no 'ntp_gate' in any .out), which is what the reviewer agent suggested from existing logs (checks/verify/reviewer/result.json, objections[10].how_to_answer and missing_from_plan[5]).
2. What exists: the end signal split off by nofc_noend; shrank while queued 9 against 288 and recompute on reading turns 585 against 2,436 (:343-344); the hold's own cost 0.006-0.019 s (:297).
3. Two earlier pieces the claim missed: the gate and hold measured alone on exact hints at 44 users (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:117, -0.17 s, 4 %; :157, interval +0.03 to +0.41 s, a 75 min run), and a log attribution of the old hint-free arm's losses at 128 users (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:169-183: queued history evicted on 36 % of returning turns; refused reads never retried carry over 80 % of the recompute; pacing 'follows the losses rather than causing them').
4. Feasibility of arms without an engine edit: gate and hold are on/off flags (frozen/engine_ec_20261111e/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/memory.py:331-355) and queue lines take extra flags (scripts/start_server.sh:186-189); queued-turn protection is the eviction score. Re-reads have no flag (MAX_REFETCHES = 2, next_turn_prefetch.py:108), so a 're-reads off' arm needs a new freeze. No validation hook I read refuses 'arrival' timing with gate and hold off, but I did not run the validator.
5. A log attribution at 44 users takes seconds with existing scripts. My read-only run of checks/limits/why_recompute.py and recompute.py on hintfree_ctl (output only in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-wanhr-sglang/7c93b1d5-dc1c-431d-8d3e-efb4ae23a30d/scratchpad/audit/verify-u53-56/why_recompute_hintfree_ctl.out and /tmp/claude-1001/-home-wanhr-sglang/7c93b1d5-dc1c-431d-8d3e-efb4ae23a30d/scratchpad/audit/verify-u53-56/recompute_hintfree_ctl.out): 534 turns recompute 4K+ tokens against 113 in nofc_noend; read refused room 178 (1.0 refusals each, so never retried) against 50 (2.1); found on SSD but read little 157 against 4; read then lost before admission 95 against 22; shrank markers 316 against 10. In nofc_noend's own log the gate decided covered 5,029, read 2,149, reread 613, capped 4, with 165 ntp_hold and 245 ntp_reevict events (my grep counts).
6. Stale, on the held list: PAPER_PLAN.md:7 ('a hint-free engine with those three is untested') and :27 (option I 'is the rival a reviewer will ask for'); both have now run as nofc_noend and nofc_noend_c128. The ladder steps of :18 are still not run.
verdict.who_reason: Separating the mechanisms by arms is new GPU time and a queue change, always the user's call. The log attribution needs no GPU and is not on the held list, but nobody asked for it: 'not yet separated' at DECISIONS.md:219 pointed at the nofc_noend arm, which ran, and the record promises no further split.
verdict.recommended_action: Ask the user one question: do they want the three mechanisms separated, and at which setting (44 users and 70 GB, where the bundle is 1.0 s, or 128 users). Offer two sizes: (a) about half an hour of CPU, a DECISIONS entry from the commands of point 5 (from agent_cache/: nice -n 10 python3 -I -B results/campaign26/checks/limits/why_recompute.py 20261111_045808_three_tier_wc_dl_poll0_custom_L1nat_H70 20261111_130801_three_tier_wc_oracle_v2_nu_owned_custom_L1nat_H70, the same with recompute.py, and the ntp_gate, ntp_hold and ntp_reevict counts), citing CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:117 and :169-183; (b) two arms of 2 h on the frozen engine e, the nofc_noend line with gate and hold off, and with the eviction score back to plain LRU, each checked first with checks/validate_queue.py. A 're-reads off' arm waits for a new freeze.
verdict.risk: Nothing may be appended to queue.txt without the user's word: c26.sh re-reads it after every arm, so a new line would run. The log attribution reads finished logs only. Its limit: it counts losses by class, it is not causal, and the hint-free control also differs from nofc_noend in engine build (engine_5df71c4bf0_v2 against engine_ec_20261111e, queue.txt), so build and mechanisms cannot be told apart from logs alone.

items.title: Rule 3 was not compared with a Bidaw-style eviction, which PAPER_INTRO.md says it has to be; other prior systems are not built as rivals
items.what_is_undone: PAPER_INTRO.md says the planned rule 3 'has to be compared with' Bidaw's hit potential (L183-184), that the strongest hint-free baseline includes Bidaw's read order (waiting time over KV size, L120), and that contribution 3 stays a promise until then (L109-110). Campaign 26 compared rule 3 with next use from the p50, ended-first LRU and queue-only LRU; the engine's scores are entry, samples, lru and queue, and storage reads dispatch in deadline order. 'Bidaw' appears in DECISIONS.md at L32 only. Also not built as rivals (reviewer): CachedAttention's look-ahead, Continuum's TTL rule (closest is score samples, never run), Tokencake beyond the point-timed JIT p50 arms. Missing: the comparison, or a decision that it is not needed because four eviction scores came out level once reads hold little room (L982-984). An offline version (a Bidaw-style score in evict_replay.py) would need no GPU, but its fidelity needs the paper.
items.sources: Finders: record-1, paper-plan; notes of record-2 and paper-plan. PAPER_INTRO.md:107-110, 119-120, 183-184 ('Probabilistic next-use eviction: Bidaw's hit potential. Planned rule 3 has to be compared with it, not only with LRU and point forecasts.'); DECISIONS.md:32, 982-984; python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/next_use_eviction.py:61 (RETURN_SCORES: entry, samples, lru, queue); reviewer result.json.
items.why_who: It needs new engine code and arms, or the user's choice to answer it in text; the record never puts the question. Effort: one paragraph to argue it away; a replay study about half a day; an engine score plus one 2 h arm about a day.

verdict.evidence:
The comparison does not exist and no decision about it is recorded.
- Record: `grep -i bidaw` on results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md hits line 32 only ("... the queue-aware hint-free rival is not built | fixed-quantile rival is a flag; the rest is open").
- Engine: `RETURN_SCORES = ("entry", "samples", "lru", "queue")` (python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/next_use_eviction.py:61); reads dispatch "earliest deadline first" (storage_read_scheduler.py:6, :100).
- Replay: the policies of frozen/ec_policy_20261111/evict_replay/evict_replay.py:275-286 are LRU, ended-first LRU, exact, next use from the p50, return chance, samples and hazard. No file under agent_cache/ other than PAPER_INTRO.md and DECISIONS.md:32 names Bidaw or a hit-potential score.
- PAPER_INTRO.md:183-184 ("Planned rule 3 has to be compared with it, not only with LRU and point forecasts"), :109-110 and :119-120 read as the claim quotes them. The reviewer agent says the same (checks/verify/reviewer/result.json, objections[10] and missing_from_plan[5]); the 12 points at DECISIONS.md:491-506 do not carry it by name.
- The user was told only that the deck's reference slide omits the four citations (transcript line 23049, 2026-11-11T04:35:28Z). No user prompt of 11-13 Nov asks for the comparison, and the deck's own method list and next steps (slides "methods" and "next") have no Bidaw-style rival. So it is a requirement the lead wrote into PAPER_INTRO.md on 6 Nov, not part of the campaign 26 request.

One part of the claim is overstated. The CachedAttention-style rival that PAPER_INTRO.md:204-206 asks for ("Build that arm and present it as the CachedAttention-style baseline", option I at CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:303) was built and run as `nofc_noend` (DECISIONS.md:318-356, :358-360, with a repeat and a 128-user run), and PAPER_INTRO.md:105-106 and :194 treat JIT p50 as Tokencake's class of rule. What has no stand-in is Bidaw's eviction and read order, and Continuum's TTL.

Evidence on need, which is not a decision: four eviction scores are level at 44 users and 70 GB (DECISIONS.md:981-985); the `samples` score, the nearest thing to a learned reuse-distance score, was left unqueued as "worth less than one run can show" (:126-127); the read thread is 16-20 % busy there (:290), so a read order has little to reorder.

Side note: PAPER_INTRO.md:212 says `lit.md` section 8 "is not on this machine". A `lit.md` is at agent_cache/frozen/hint_realism_20261027/reports/lit.md (27 Oct, sections 0-4, no section 8, no mention of Bidaw), so the section 8 that PAPER_PLAN.md:7 cites is not in it.
verdict.who_reason: Nobody asked for it in campaign 26 and the lead never promised it. A Bidaw-style score in the engine means a new freeze and a GPU arm, and settling it in text means editing the paper docs, which are held.
verdict.recommended_action: Put it to the user as one question with three answers and the evidence above: argue it in the paper from the level eviction scores; add a Bidaw-style policy to a copy of `evict_replay.py` under results/campaign26/checks/limits/ (CPU, about 30 s per timeline, the way `pool_sweep.py` reuses the replay); or build the score and run one 2 h arm after the queue. The replay route needs Bidaw's exact rule, and only the one-row summary at PAPER_INTRO.md:172 is on this machine.
verdict.risk: None in asking. The replay route reads finished runs only. An engine score cannot go into the frozen engines and needs GPU time, so it waits for the queue and for the user.

items.title: The engine has never resolved a hint from its own reply in a GPU run
items.what_is_undone: The deck's session slide says the key is read from the engine's own reply; PAPER_PLAN.md:17 still carries 'the engine has never read its own reply on a GPU'. Campaign 26 does not remove the caveat: the client sends replay_reply_key, the recorded reply's key, as a stand-in, and every run checked has reply_key_source 'hint' (server_args.txt of runs 20261111_070012, 20261112_194449 and 20261113_192822). The engine's own-reply path (next_turn_prefetch.py:575-580) has unit coverage only. With this replay the generated reply differs from the recorded one, so a direct test needs a live agent or a forced-reply mode. The reviewer also asked for an arm with the reply key parsed by the engine.
items.sources: Finders: deck, paper-plan; record-2 (in its seeds item). Deck slide session 'The hint arrives with each request; the key is read from the engine's own reply.'; scripts/replay_agentic.py:24-25 'replay_reply_key stands in for the engine reading its own reply: it is the recorded reply's key'; PAPER_PLAN.md:17; DECISIONS.md:505.
items.why_who: Engine and client work outside the four rules, frozen during the campaign; a gap older than campaign 26; or a decision to state it as a limit in the paper. Effort unclear: a live-agent demo is days, a forced-reply replay mode is a client and engine change.

verdict.evidence:

items.title: Rule 2 lacks the deck's due-time comparison
items.what_is_undone: As built, an arrived turn's read takes room from the staged read with the lowest chance of return within its own read time (soft_pin_victims sorts staged reads by chance_within alone). The deck adds that strictly the two due times are compared, and its toy puts up to 20 % on not bumping a history due back sooner than its own re-read; that guard is not in soft_pin_victims. In ec_full 163 of 462 bumped turns arrived within 5 s and 452 read again, which is where the 27 % extra SSD pages come from. No check says how many bumps the guard would have stopped (countable from ec_bump lines and arrivals, about 1 h of CPU, if wanted).

items.why_who: An engine change, frozen during the campaign, and only worth it if rule 2 stays in the paper. Effort: half a day for the engine change.

verdict.evidence:
Rule 2 is built in the form the plan states; the deck's strict form is not, and nothing records the difference.

Built: PAPER_PLAN.md:104 ("take it from the staged read with the lowest F_j(r_j | t)") and :168, and the slide's main line.

Not built:

- The toy's guard: "up to 20 percent less again when an arrived turn does not bump a history that is due back sooner than its own re-read would take" (slide floor, notes; agent_cache/scripts/toy_floor.py:286 and :414, `arrivals == "compete"`).
- In the engine, `soft_pin_victims` sorts staged reads by `chance_within` over their own read time and takes them in that order until the shortfall is covered, with no test against the asking turn's due time and no threshold (python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/next_turn_prefetch.py:1227-1240).

Not recorded: DECISIONS.md:61 says only "`--hicache-storage-next-turn-soft-pins on`: rule 2". The phrase "two due times" occurs in the transcript only where the deck was read on 11 Nov, never in a message to the user, and results/campaign26/checks/bumps.py does not count it.

A rough count from `ec_full`'s server.log (mine, 0.3 s of CPU; `bump_guard.py` and `bump_guard.out` in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-wanhr-sglang/7c93b1d5-dc1c-431d-8d3e-efb4ae23a30d/scratchpad/audit/verify-u57-u60/):
- The turn the room went to asked for it a median 0.04 s after arriving and was admitted a median 1.23 s after the bump (p90 3.37 s; more than 5 s after in 22 of 458). So at this setting the arrived turn is due about one read time later, and the slide's long-queue case is rare.
- In hindsight the bumped turn arrived before that admission in 76 of 458 bumps, and was back within its own re-read time plus the engine's 1 s margin in 59 of 462.
- By the engine's own forecast, 67 of 462 bumps had a chance of 0.5 or more, and 20 of those were right.
- So a due-time guard would have stopped about one bump in six at most: 2-3 % of the run's SSD pages, against the 14 % that bumps cost (checks/bumps.out). It would not change how `ec_full` reads.

If the number is to be quoted, redo it as a proper check (a few lines added to results/campaign26/checks/bumps.py, run on `ec_full` against `ec_r134`). Leave the engine alone.

items.title: Rule 3 is built without the reload cost factor, and the record does not say so
items.what_is_undone: The plan and the deck formula score eviction by the chance of return times the cost per token to bring the history back (SSD read, or recompute for holes; the deck's c of 47 or 110 us per token). ReturnChanceStrategy.get_priority ranks by the chance alone and reads no price, so there is no keep test either. 'What was built' and the review table never mention the factor. PAPER_PLAN gives a reason it may not matter (histories read back whole from SSD share one cost), but the same strategy also orders GPU eviction, where the way back is a host copy. Open: is the paper's rule 3 the chance alone, or is the factor built and measured. The one-line record note is in U2.

items.title: Paper docs: the intro's SSD-bandwidth framing is not what limits the campaign 26 settings
items.what_is_undone: The opening (L19-21) and 'Still new' (L187-189) sell timing SSD reads before arrival 'on a saturated device'. At both campaign 26 settings the SSD is not the limit: the read thread is 16-20 % busy at 44 users, a read at arrival costs about 1.2 s on the 5-10 % of turns that read (0.06 s per turn), and at 128 users the queue wait covers the read. The limit found is host room for an arrived turn's read. The framing may still hold at x70, which has no run of the new arms (U42).
items.sources: Finder: paper-plan. PAPER_INTRO.md:19-21, 187-189 ('Timing SSD reads before arrival on a saturated device whose bandwidth reads and writes share.'); DECISIONS.md:290 ('The SSD is not the limit.'), 554-558, 687-689, 1026-1027.
items.why_who: The intro rewrite is held; whether to keep the x70 framing depends on the x70 decision.

verdict.evidence:
The wording is in the intro: PAPER_INTRO.md:19-21 "reading at arrival puts the slowest tier on the critical path. In our setup a returning turn reads about 1.6 GB [x70], so an SSD that sustains about 2 GB/s ... brings back a little over one turn per second"; :187 "Timing SSD reads before arrival on a saturated device whose bandwidth reads and writes share."; :216-217 "a tier that takes seconds per history and is already saturated".

But the doc already limits the claim, which is why this is only partly undone. The opening's numbers are marked "[x70]", and :76-78 says "At x10 (campaign 19, analysed 2026-11-05) the trigger was spent retry budgets, with the SSD far from saturated (reads 0.53, writes 0.64 GB/s). At 128 users the baseline recomputes 3,784 tokens per turn while its SSD is 39-48 % busy". Only :187 and :216-217 say "saturated" with no scope.

What campaign 26 adds and the intro lacks: DECISIONS.md:290 "**The SSD is not the limit.** The read thread is busy 16-20 % of these runs and at most 55 % of any 5 minutes."; :291-294 the room is; :554-558 a read at arrival costs about 1.2 s on the 5-10 % of turns that read, 0.06 s per turn; :687-689 "the next gain at this setting is room for an arrived turn's read ... not the timing of early reads"; :1025-1027 "The setting cannot rank read-start rules: the queue wait covers the read."; :1086-1088 at 100 GB the reads themselves go.

A qualifier the claim misses: at 128 users the SSD is busy, it just does not decide TTFT. The arms read 998K to 1,441K pages there (DECISIONS.md:785, :1005), and PAPER_INTRO.md:86-87 has the device "47-78 % busy instead of 97-98 %". So the framing is untested for the new arms, not contradicted.

items.title: Paper docs: the written formulation differs from what was built and measured
items.what_is_undone: The plan's 'Formulation' still describes the deck's policy. The build departs from it in at least six places, so the paper's math would not describe the measured system: (1) rule 3 scores GPU and host eviction, while the formulation leaves GPU eviction to HiCache (L82); (2) a staged read's pin is given back once its entry has passed, while the formulation has no release (L106); (3) rent is charged on every token of the key not in GPU memory, not on the tokens the read holds; (4) the predicted wait counts the queue only while a turn with nothing to read has stayed queued 0.5 s; (5) the price that ran is the harm rule, not the dual-ascent rule 4; (6) the hint is a two-piece lognormal through p10/p50/p90, not a histogram with an 'ended' bin. Other readers add: rule 3 has no cost factor (U61) and rule 1's read time is the load model's estimate plus a 1 s margin (U13). Rows are missing too: the 100 GB setting in the resources table and the two forecast-free rivals in the methods table.
items.sources: Finder: paper-plan. PAPER_PLAN.md:36-46, 82 ('GPU eviction and admission order stay as HiCache does them.'), 98-108, 112-120, 137; DECISIONS.md:23 ('rule 3 scores every session in GPU and host memory'), 25, 49, 72-79 ('so it is now charged on every token of the key not in GPU memory.'), 196.

verdict.evidence:
Every listed departure holds, checked in the plan and in the code at HEAD (python/ is clean against a5fe6121c8), and the list is short by five.

1. GPU eviction: PAPER_PLAN.md:82 "GPU eviction and admission order stay as HiCache does them." Build: DECISIONS.md:23 "rule 3 scores every session in GPU and host memory".
2. Release: none in PAPER_PLAN.md:94-104. Build: next_turn_prefetch.py:126 `NTP_RELEASE_GRACE_S = 5.0`, used at :1082 (DECISIONS.md:25).
3. Rent: next_turn_prefetch.py:1106 `plan.room_tokens = len(plan.key) - in_device`, :1117 `rent_per_s=self._price.price * plan.room_tokens`.
4. Wait: next_turn_prefetch.py:668-682, the queue counts only once a request with no read under way has waited `NTP_GPU_BOUND_S = 0.5` (:129); plan :102 says "queue position over admission rate".
5. Price: the queue.txt lines of ec_r134, ec_r134_c128 and ec_full carry `--hicache-storage-next-turn-price-learning harm` (DECISIONS.md:196); plan :108 is the dual-ascent form, never run. At 128 users the price never moved (DECISIONS.md:792-796), where plan :131 expects "λ ≈ 0".
6. Hint form: next_turn_policy.py:55-56 "the two-piece lognormal through an entry's p10, p50 and p90". Plan :137 calls the histogram "the lean" under "Open", so this is a blank to fill more than a contradiction.

Beyond the six:
7. Rule 3 has no cost factor: next_use_eviction.py:258 `return (RETURN_TIER_SCORED, chance, idle - dist.median_s)`; plan :106 has F_i(H | t) c_i.
8. Read time: next_turn_prefetch.py:1165-1167, load estimate plus `NTP_JIT_MARGIN_S` (1.0 s, :117); plan :98 has r_i = b L_i / β.
9. Not built: per-key recalibration in rule 4 (DECISIONS.md:63) and rule 3's keep test against the price.
10. Plan :98-102 says the read "lands at the newsvendor quantile ... 8K-token read lands at p29 ... 64K at p77". The deck's slide 18 now says "It is not a landing quantile." By the plan's own start rule the read lands at percentile q + (1 - q)·Φ(start); I re-derived it. The same reading sits at PAPER_PLAN.md:130, :149, :167, :189 and PAPER_INTRO.md:95.
11. Tables and steps: PAPER_PLAN.md:36-46 has no 100 GB column; :112-120 has no row for nofc or nofc_noend and still says "Fixed quantile (rival, not run)" (fq90 ran, DECISIONS.md:883) and "Expected cost (proposed)"; :201-204 lists building rule 1 and its GPU arms as "Next".

critic_items.title: The engine's arrival-offset estimate absorbs forecast error under three-quantile hints; it now sets the idle clock of rules 1 to 3; unrecorded
critic_items.what_is_undone: The engine keeps a running estimate of delivery delay (arrival minus commit minus the hinted gap) and folds in every arrival whose value is between 0 and 5 s. With exact hints that is delivery delay. With table hints the hinted gap is the p50, so the value is forecast error, and only the positive errors under 5 s are kept. Measured on campaign 26's logs by this reader: the estimate is 0.11 s at the median with exact hints (jit_exact_d, p90 0.25 s) and 0.36-0.44 s with table hints (jit_p50_d, ec_r13, ec_r1, nofc_noend, ec_r134_c128; p90 0.74-0.84 s, max 1.6-1.9 s), with 53-57 % of arrivals folded in. The 4 Nov audit found this, sized the fix at 'a few lines and one unit test' (update the offset from exact plans only) and noted it was recorded nowhere; it was told to the user that day. In engines d and e the estimate also feeds rule 1's idle time, rule 2's chance of return, rule 3's idle_from and the samples the engine would collect per key, so those clocks run about 0.3 s behind in every hinted arm. DECISIONS.md does not mention it ('offset' occurs nowhere), nor does 'Known and left'. Missing: one line in the record, the table saved under checks/, and after the campaign the fix (the user's call). Its effect on TTFT is unmeasured; it is small beside rule 1's 1.0 s margin (U13).

critic_items.title: Real-system parts that no run or test exercises, beyond the engine reading its own reply (U58)
critic_items.what_is_undone: Listed to the user on 4 Nov as 'the real-system half, never exercised' and still so after campaign 26, whose no-hint rival also depends on two of them. (1) Linking: the engine ties a request to its session's plan by a next request id the client names in advance; the replay knows it, a real harness does not, and plans would have to key by session. (2) Session end: a finish call or a reply with no tool call has no 'ended' entry; the replay sends the key _end. Only nofc_noend runs without the end signal; no pricing arm does (U50). (3) kv_hints is read by the OpenAI chat path only; the Anthropic messages adapter does not carry it. (4) The prefetcher refuses any setup with more than one rank (TP or PP above 1, DP attention, PD disaggregation), so every result is one GPU. (5) The table: kept across restarts, aged, sent as changes (3 KB per request today). From the reviewer's list, also uncarried: a client that reports short gaps to keep its history in memory at other tenants' cost. Missing: a decision whether any of these is built or tested, or each is stated as a limit in the paper.

critic_items.title: What the tool-category key is worth has never been measured on the GPU
critic_items.what_is_undone: The paper plan lists the conditional table (an entry per tool and command word, picked by the engine from its reply) as a contribution. Its value is shown offline only (AUC 0.69 against 0.52 for the tool alone at x10). The contrast needs no engine change: HINT_KEY=none gives every turn one table-wide entry. It has never run: all 16 table-hint runs of campaign 26 use hint_key command, and the reviewer's contradicted claim 9 says no arm contrasts three quantiles with one number under the new rules. With the no-hint rival level with rules 1 and 3 the expected difference is small, so a single arm may show nothing; the question is whether to run it (under rules 1 and 3, 44 users, 70 GB) or to drop the key from the paper's claims. c26.sh does not pass HINT_KEY, so an arm needs a launcher variant after the queue ends, as another seed does (U44). The CPU check of the pooled limit (U15) is the offline half.
